weekend_note: Dry and warm Wednesday and Thursday, then rain builds: about 60 percent Friday night, 70 percent Saturday and 60 percent Sunday. The National Hurricane Center is also watching a Gulf system, so check forecasts. Indoor picks: Postmodern Jukebox Thursday and Daniel Tosh Friday at the Saenger, plus the Glass and Ceramic Pumpkin Patch. Festa Italiana and the beach songwriters weekend are mostly outdoors.

news.title: NHC watching Gulf system that could become a tropical depression
news.summary: The Hurricane Center gives a low-pressure area in the southwestern Gulf high odds of developing this week, with heavy rain on saturated ground as the main concern.

news.title: Downtown Pensacola parking rates change Oct. 5
news.summary: Sunday and Monday are free, paid parking runs Tuesday through Friday at $1 an hour, and Friday night and Saturday are $1.75 an hour. Seniors 65 and up can buy a monthly pass.

news.title: Emerald Coast PBS to launch Nov. 1
news.summary: A new nonprofit will bring PBS and PBS KIDS back to Northwest Florida on channels 53.1 and 53.2 after Pensacola State College ended its affiliation in July.

news.title: ECUA to replace Monteigne Drive sewer main
news.summary: A roughly $2 million project starting Oct. 12 follows a July overflow and is set to finish in January.

news.title: School bus driver shortage causes daily delays
news.summary: The district reported 18 open driver jobs in mid-September, with some students waiting over an hour; nine drivers have been hired since July.

coverage_note: Weather is the NWS detailed forecast issued 3 AM CDT Oct 6 for the Pensacola area; it covers Oct 6 to 11 only, since the Oct 12 low was not given. Several sources (Saenger, Visit Pensacola, PensacolaBeach.com, Blue Wahoos, Bay Center and Local Pulse's newest post) would not load this run, so events past Oct 11 rely on Must Do Pensacola and earlier reads, and Saenger shows after Oct 9 were not confirmed. Restaurant statuses are unchanged and Pelican Bar and Grill is still unconfirmed. NorthEscambia.com article pages would not load, so north and west Escambia coverage is headline-only; a Molino ballpark Halloween tournament was seen in a headline but without dates, so it is not listed. Gonzalez and Perdido Key listings are thin, and Facebook-only events are not covered.
